item.title: Oil Prices Rise as Hormuz Shipping Risks Persist
item.description: While renewed escalation could push crude prices higher, confirmation of direct U.S.-Iran talks at this week’s U.N. General Assembly could weigh on prices by raising expectations for increased supply.

item.title: U.K. Government Borrowing Rose in August as Budget Looms
item.description: The U.K. government borrowed more in August than a year earlier, a setback for its plans to reduce its deficit as it prepares to outline a new budget next month.

item.title: In the Baltics, NATO Forces Are Trying to Learn the New Way of War
item.description: As Canadian-led troops in Latvia adapt lessons from the war in Ukraine, a big gap remains.

item.title: In Trump, Xi Sees ‘Rare Window’ to Convince Taiwan That Resistance Is Futile
item.description: Beijing is courting Taiwan’s opposition—and quietly helped stage its leader’s landmark visit to the mainland—to pull the island into its orbit.

item.title: Iran’s President Gets Rare Opportunity to Make His Case to the World
item.description: Masoud Pezeshkian is expected to speak at the United Nations on Wednesday, giving him a platform to rail against the U.S. and try to sway the world to Iran’s side.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Spent Months Trying to Bypass Hormuz. Now There’s No Way Around It.
item.description: With its Red Sea bypass route disrupted by attacks from Yemen and Iraq, the world’s oil kingpin is returning to the waterway it was trying to avoid in the first place.

item.title: Canada to Enshrine Expedited Project Reviews With Legislation
item.description: The legislation also attempts to minimize labor disruptions in key trade-focused parts of the economy like railways and ports.

item.title: British Columbia Sues OpenAI, Alleging ChatGPT Aided Mass School Shooting
item.description: The lawsuit alleges that the AI company failed to notify law enforcement and calls out product safety gaps.

item.title: Oil Prices Fall for Fourth Day as Supply Concerns Ease
item.description: Improving flows through the Strait of Hormuz and prospects for renewed diplomacy over the Iran conflict eased immediate supply concerns.

item.title: U.S. Proposes $5 Billion to Kickstart Fund to Rebuild Gulf Energy Sites
item.description: The proposal is under discussion with several Middle Eastern countries including Saudi Arabia and U.A.E.

item.title: Why Helicopter Parents in China Buy Watches, Not Phones, for Their Kids
item.description: Children’s smartwatches are hugely popular in China for preteens, with some models offering advanced location tracking

item.title: Germany’s Merz Pledges to Stay On Despite ‘Disastrous’ Election Result
item.description: The German chancellor pledged to forge ahead with an unpopular economic overhaul despite his collapsing popularity and a string of electoral routs.

item.description: The agreement doesn’t deliver the control he wanted, but it raises hopes of more investment and less local stigma around working with America.

item.title: Trump Ramps Up Bid to Dismantle International Criminal Court
item.description: The U.S. administration is preparing sweeping sanctions that would cut the court off from much of the global financial system.
